implementation_notes: std::sync::mpsc is generic over the message type: let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Order>() creates a channel that cannot carry anything but Order, so the receiver's loop needs no type dispatch, Sender is cloneable for several producers while Receiver serves exactly one consumer - which matches one channel per type with one consumer group. sync_channel(bound) adds a bounded buffer and turns send() into backpressure; asynchronous services replace both halves with tokio::sync::mpsc, which is bounded by design (channel(capacity)) and awaits instead of blocking the thread. Where the channel crosses a process boundary the Rust types disappear, so the topic/queue name plus a serde enum per message type take over the binding.
pitfalls: std::sync::mpsc::channel is unbounded: a fast producer with a slow consumer grows memory until the process dies, so use sync_channel(bound) or reach for the async runtime's bounded channel.
Receiver is Send but not Sync - one consumer per channel; serving a type from several threads needs a Mutex around the receiver or a different structure (crossbeam-channel, a runtime channel).
When the receiver is dropped, send() returns Err(SendError) and hands the payload back: ignoring that error loses messages silently at shutdown.

variants.name: tokio::sync::mpsc bounded async channel
variants.implementation_notes: In an async service the same per-type binding lives in tokio::sync::mpsc: channel(capacity) is bounded from the start, send().await yields instead of blocking the executor, and recv().await returns None when every sender is dropped - so shutdown and backpressure are part of the type rather than a hand-rolled convention. Capacity is mandatory (zero panics), which forces the per-type buffer decision into the code, and the same Sender/Receiver split (many senders, one receiver) still models one consumer group per message type. Prefer it over std::sync::mpsc whenever producers or consumers are tasks rather than threads.
pitfalls: The buffer capacity is mandatory and must be at least 1: tokio::sync::mpsc::channel(0) panics, so an accidental zero once the size becomes configurable is a startup crash.
Holding a std::sync::Mutex across send().await blocks the executor; the async channel plus a small critical section is the alternative.
